answer: Sybil resistance here rests on a per-agent registration bond posted from a spender cleared by the last epoch's challenge. One extra identity costs a fresh bond plus the steady spend needed to keep answering, so a thousand fake agents cost a thousand bonds and a thousand live cycles while real work is paid once. Idle clusters lose both their spendable pool and their pulse. Attackers face a rising per-identity charge, like a harbor fee per hull, so flooding the ledger is priced out; a lone sparrow cannot cheaply impersonate a flock, since each mock bird must post its own collateral.
